data.narrative:
Type One Energy, a Series B-stage nuclear energy company founded by David Anderson, Chris Hegna, and John Canik, is evaluated against a universe of 11 peers—3 public and 8 private—spanning the nuclear energy sector, including comparable entities such as Helion, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach. Using the company's $100M+ total raised as a proxy baseline, a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement yields an implied valuation of $190M. This method applies where peer-median analysis is insufficiently supported: while 6 same-sector peers exist, none of the narrow filters—same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparables—yielded the minimum 3 datapoints required for robust median derivation. A direct peer-median cross-check was therefore deemed misleading and excluded.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $162M to $218M, centered on $190M. Key uncertainties include the absence of a sufficiently dense peer cohort at identical stage and valuation tier, limiting cross-validation of the stage-progression result. The single-method foundation reflects genuine scarcity in close nuclear energy comparables at Series B, a characteristic risk to navigation in frontier-tech sectors. Additional clarity on revenue run-rate, capital intensity, and regulatory pathway would refine confidence in the upper and lower bounds.
